raw_case_text:
A 43-year-old man was admitted to the our hospital because of relapsed non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. Since three years ago, he had been treated with 8th cycles of ProMACE-CytaBOM chemotherapy for diffuse mixed small and large cell type malignant lymphoma and achieved complete remission. The disease relapse was noted 27 months later and he underwent salvage chemotherapy with CDME regimen(Cisplatin, Dexamethasone, Mitoxantrone, Etoposide). On the fifth day after chemotherapy, he developed fever and diarrhea and was diagnosed as fungal sepsis for Candida tropicalis and was treated with intravenous amphotericin B administration. On the following day, he developed sudden onset of abdominal pain and massive intestinal bleeding. On physical examination, breathing sounds were normal and abdomen was distended and tympanic with infrequent bowel sound. There was diffuse and mild tenderness on abdomen without rebound tenderness or muscle guarding. A rectal examination revealed melena. Laboratory finding revealed WBC 4,000/mm3 (neutrophils 84.7%, lymphocytes 5.0%, monocytes 9.8%), hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, platelet 173,000/mm3. Blood and urine cultures showed no growth of bacteria and gastrointestinal bleeding was persisting. On the twenty-fifth hospital day, we performed gastrofiberscopy and total colonoscopy. On endoscopic findings, the discrete ulcerations, white patches and multiple erythema of distal esophagus and lesser curvature of stomach body portion were found, active bleeding is not noted. Endoscopic biopsy were performed in ulcer base and margin of esophagus and stomach. On total colonoscopic findings, there were only old blood clots in large bowel. 99mTc-RBC abdominal scan showed accumulation of radionuclide in left lower quadrant on 24 hours delayed scaning. It suggested bleeding from small intestine. He underwent the explorating laparatomy.
In operation fields, jejunal segment of small intestine showed a diffuse inflammatory process. There were dark blood clots in distal jejunum and ileum. The involved area of the small intestine was removed and the intestinal continuity was reestablished by end to end anastomosing the upper jejunum to the terminal ileum. The resection specimen consisted of 48-cm-long portion of jejunum. Grossly, there were multiple ill-defined ulcerations surrounded by irregular nodularities of mucosa(Fig 1 a, b). On histologic examination, the ulcer base was consisted of necrotic exudate and granulation tissue. Also, on HE stain, there was many enlarged cells with purple intranuclear inclusions surrounded by a clear halo and smaller basophilic cytoplasmic inclusion mainly in the submucosa and muscle layer of ulcerative areas. It suggested the cytomegalovirus infection of jejunum(Fig 2 a). On histologic examination of endoscopic biopsy specimen of esophagus and stomach, there were small basophilic inclusion bodies in endothelial cells and glandular cells(Fig 2 b). In our case, we performed the immunohistochemical staining to detect pp65 antigen of CMV in cytospin preparations of peripheral blood neutrophils(Fig 3 a) and paraffin-embedded surgical specimen of jejunum by the APAAP(alkaline phosphatase antialkaline phosphatase)(Clonal CMVKit, Biotest, Germany) method(Fig 3 b). Also, IF stain using DAKO-CMV, DDG9 and CCH2(DAKO, USA) for immediate early CMV antigen was performed from urine shell vial culture which showed heavy CMV infection.
After surgical resection of jejunum, he treated with gancyclovir for three weeks. He was improved and GI bleeding had stopped in post operation 1 day and has been followed at the out-patient clinic.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 43-year-old man with relapsed non-Hodgkin's lymphoma developed fever and diarrhea on day 5 after salvage CDME chemotherapy, followed the next day by sudden-onset abdominal pain and massive lower gastrointestinal bleeding.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Initially achieving complete remission of diffuse mixed small and large cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma 3 years prior after 8 cycles of ProMACE-CytaBOM chemotherapy, the patient relapsed 27 months later and was admitted for salvage CDME chemotherapy (cisplatin, dexamethasone, mitoxantrone, etoposide). On day 5 post-chemotherapy, he developed fever and diarrhea with Candida tropicalis fungemia (treated with IV amphotericin B), and on day 6 he experienced acute abdominal pain and massive, persistent melena/intestinal hemorrhage.
subjective.past_medical_history: Relapsed diffuse mixed small and large cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (diagnosed 3 years prior, relapsed after 27-month first remission) status post 8 cycles of ProMACE-CytaBOM and salvage CDME chemotherapy; intercurrent Candida tropicalis fungal sepsis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, diarrhea, sudden-onset diffuse abdominal pain, abdominal distension, and massive persistent melena.

objective.physical_examination: Normal breath sounds; distended, tympanic abdomen with infrequent bowel sounds and mild diffuse abdominal tenderness without rebound tenderness or muscular guarding; digital rectal examination revealed frank melena.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC 4,000/mm3 (84.7% neutrophils, 5.0% lymphocytes, 9.8% monocytes), hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, platelets 173,000/mm3; initial blood culture positive for Candida tropicalis (subsequent bacterial blood and urine cultures negative).
objective.advanced_workup: Hospital day 25 gastrofiberscopy showed discrete ulcerations, white patches, and erythema in the distal esophagus and lesser curvature of the gastric body without active bleeding; total colonoscopy showed old blood clots throughout the colon without a colonic bleeding source. Technetium-99m RBC scintigraphy demonstrated tracer accumulation in the left lower quadrant on 24-hour delayed imaging, localizing hemorrhage to the small intestine. Exploratory laparotomy with resection of a 48-cm segment of inflamed jejunum (and end-to-end jejunoileal anastomosis) revealed multiple ill-defined jejunal ulcers surrounded by irregular mucosal nodularity. Histopathology (H&E) demonstrated ulcer bases with necrotic exudate/granulation tissue and numerous enlarged cytomegalic cells containing purple intranuclear inclusions surrounded by a clear halo and smaller basophilic cytoplasmic inclusions in the jejunal submucosa and muscularis propria, as well as small basophilic inclusions in esophageal and gastric endothelial and glandular cells. Active CMV infection was confirmed by positive CMV pp65 antigen immunohistochemical staining (APAAP method, Clonal CMVKit) in peripheral blood neutrophils and resected jejunal tissue, and positive immediate-early CMV antigen immunofluorescence (DAKO DDG9/CCH2) in urine shell vial culture.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of multifocal gastrointestinal cytomegalovirus (CMV) disease (esophagitis, gastritis, and ulcerative jejunitis) presenting with massive jejunal hemorrhage in a patient with relapsed non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, confirmed by characteristic intranuclear and intracytoplasmic CMV inclusions in resected jejunum and gastroesophageal biopsies, positive CMV pp65 APAAP immunostaining in peripheral blood neutrophils and jejunal tissue, and positive urine shell vial culture immunofluorescence. Treated with emergency segmental jejunal resection (48 cm) followed by a 3-week course of intravenous ganciclovir, achieving immediate cessation of GI bleeding on postoperative day 1 and sustained recovery on outpatient follow-up.
